findings.title: Verify ignores session expiry
findings.description: Verify returns any matching session without checking ExpiresAt, so expired tokens keep working contrary to its documented contract.

findings.title: RequireAdmin always returns true
findings.description: Both branches return true, so non-admin sessions are accepted as administrators.

findings.title: BearerToken crashes on malformed header
findings.description: Header.Split(' ') then indexing parts[1] throws IndexOutOfRangeException when there is no space/token.

findings.title: Sweep mutates dictionary during enumeration
findings.description: foreach over entries.Keys then Remove inside the loop throws InvalidOperationException.

findings.title: Utilization always truncates to zero
findings.description: Integer division entries.Count / limit * 100 is zero until count reaches limit.

findings.title: Eviction does not pick least recently used entry
findings.description: Set evicts entries.Keys.First() instead of the entry with the oldest Used timestamp.

findings.title: Bad LINKD_PORT overwrites default with zero
findings.description: int.TryParse writes 0 to cfg.Port on failure, discarding the 8080 default.

findings.title: Bad LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS still overwrites default
findings.description: cfg.Timeout is set from ms (zero) even when parsing fails, despite the log saying default kept.

findings.title: Cache TTL treated as seconds, not milliseconds
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is documented as milliseconds but parsed with TimeSpan.FromSeconds.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: parsed value is discarded; cfg.FetchLimit keeps its default.

findings.title: LoadFile throws on non-integer cache_size
findings.description: int.Parse is unguarded, so a malformed config file aborts loading.

findings.title: Validate always returns true
findings.description: Even invalid configurations are reported as valid, defeating startup validation.

findings.title: ExportCsvAsync ignores input and is async void
findings.description: Writes only the header without the links and loses exceptions via async void.

findings.title: Divide by zero when store is empty
findings.description: store.TotalHits() / store.Count throws DivideByZeroException with no links.

findings.title: Unguarded integer parse of ttl query
findings.description: int.Parse throws FormatException on invalid ttl, crashing the request handler.

findings.title: Unguarded integer parse of paging query
findings.description: int.Parse throws FormatException on invalid offset/size.

findings.title: Create crashes on unknown owner quota
findings.description: quota[owner] = quota[owner] + 1 throws KeyNotFoundException for a new owner.

findings.title: Resolve treats live links as expired
findings.description: Condition DateTime.Now < ExpiresAt removes and nulls links that are still valid.

findings.title: Rename validates from twice, not to
findings.description: ValidateCode is called twice on from and never on to.

findings.title: Page reads one element past the end
findings.description: end is set to count + 1, causing GetRange to read out of range.

findings.title: SuccessRate integer division loses remainder
findings.description: used / count * 100 truncates before multiplying, usually yielding 0.

findings.title: Delete does not restore owner quota
findings.description: Quota is incremented on create but never decremented on delete.

findings.title: Top sorts ascending instead of descending
findings.description: Sorts by Hits ascending, then takes first n, returning least-followed links.

findings.title: ByOwner uses substring match
findings.description: Owner.Contains(owner) matches owners containing the query, not exact owner.

findings.title: Extend revives expired links
findings.description: Expiry is overwritten unconditionally, violating documented finality.

findings.title: Quotas returns internal dictionary reference
findings.description: Mutating the returned dictionary affects the store, contrary to snapshot contract.

findings.title: ImportAll is not atomic
findings.description: Links are inserted one by one; partial failure leaves store mutated.

findings.title: Prune mutates dictionary during iteration and returns wrong count
findings.description: foreach over links.Keys then Remove throws InvalidOperationException; also returns remaining count instead of removed.

findings.title: All exposes internal links dictionary
findings.description: Returns the live dictionary, breaking ownership and encapsulation.

findings.title: Janitor mutates dictionary during iteration
findings.description: foreach over All().Keys then Remove inside throws InvalidOperationException.

findings.title: WarmCache does not wait for probes
findings.description: Task.Run calls are fire-and-forget, returning before cache is primed.

findings.title: CountForOwner throws for unknown owner
findings.description: store.Quotas()[owner] throws KeyNotFoundException when owner has no quota entry.

findings.title: sessions dictionary and Random shared without synchronization
findings.description: The sessions Dictionary and the Random instance are read/written by every request handler (Issue, Verify, Revoke, SessionCount), all invoked from Task.Run thread-pool threads. Dictionary is not thread-safe: a concurrent Issue (write) and Verify iteration can throw InvalidOperationException or silently lose entries; System.Random is also not thread-safe, so concurrent Issue calls corrupt the generator’s state. Scenario: two POSTs to create sessions at the same time interleave on sessions[session.Token]=session and on random.Next(), losing or duplicating a token.

findings.title: Thread-safety claim is false: Peek, Warm, Stats and Utilization bypass the lock
findings.description: Get/Set/Delete/Sweep synchronize on lock(this), but Peek reads entries.ContainsKey, Warm loops calling Peek+Set, Stats reads the long hits field, and Utilization reads entries.Count without any synchronization. Concurrent writes through Set/Janitor.Sweep (which mutates the dictionary while other threads read) race on the internal hash tables and the hits counter. Scenario: the janitor calls Sweep while a handler calls Peek/Get on the same code; one thread mutates the bucket array mid-read, corrupting the cache or throwing CollectionModified. Additionally Stats() reads `hits` without Interlocked/volatile, risking a torn value.

findings.title: Sweep mutates the dictionary while foreach iterates its Keys
findings.description: Sweep does `foreach (var code in entries.Keys)` and calls entries.Remove inside the loop. Dictionary does not allow structural changes during enumeration, so even on a single thread this throws InvalidOperationException; under the janitor this fires on every tick once an expired entry exists.

findings.title: AddCreated is non-atomic and Snapshot reads unsynchronized long fields
findings.description: resolved uses Interlocked, but created++, errors are plain increments and Snapshot returns (resolved, created, errors) with no memory barriers. Under concurrent AddCreated/AddResolved/Reset-style traffic, lost updates and torn/lagging reads are possible. The class comment promises all members are safe for concurrent use.

findings.title: Store has no synchronization despite concurrent callers and a background janitor
findings.description: links, quota and random are plain fields touched by every request (Create, Resolve, Rename, Delete, Page, etc.) and by Worker.StartJanitor’s timer callback. No locking exists, so concurrent Create + Resolve can corrupt the Dictionary, lose quotas, or throw. Create does quota[owner] = quota[owner] + 1, which both races on the same owner and throws KeyNotFoundException for first-time owners; Resolve mutates links (Remove/ Hits++) while other threads enumerate links.Values in Page/Top/Followed. Scenario: an expiry tick runs concurrently with a redirect resolving the same code → dictionary modified during traversal.

findings.title: Quotas() returns the live internal dictionary despite snapshot documentation
findings.description: The XML doc promises a snapshot that callers cannot mutate into the store, but Quotas returns `quota` directly. Worker.CountForOwner then does store.Quotas()[owner], which both races with concurrent quota updates and throws KeyNotFoundException for owners with zero links. External mutation can also corrupt store state.

findings.title: Janitor callback enumerates and mutates store.All() unsynchronized
findings.description: StartJanitor’s timer iterates `store.All().Keys` and calls store.All().Remove(code) while request threads are using the same dictionary via Store methods/All(). This races on the dictionary and also mutates during enumeration (the callback itself throws InvalidOperationException once it removes an expired key). No cancellation/disposal of the timer is coordinated with in-flight requests.

findings.title: WarmCache is fire-and-forget and returns before work completes
findings.description: WarmCache launches one Task.Run per link and returns immediately. The doc comment promises it returns after every probe. Unobserved tasks can throw on the thread pool; results are never awaited or cancelled. Cache.Set is safe (Cache locks), but exceptions and ordering are lost.

findings.title: CheckTargets blocks on async work with .Result
findings.description: CheckTargets calls `ProbeAsync(link.Target).Result` in a loop. If this ever runs on a thread with a single-threaded synchronization context (or a thread that owns a resource the async continuation needs), the blocked thread waits on a continuation that can never run → deadlock. Under concurrent load the sequential .Result also stalls the caller thread for the whole sweep.

findings.title: WriteSnapshot uses a hard-coded shared temp file path
findings.description: Every call writes to /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json before moving it. Concurrent snapshot requests overwrite the same temp file, so one process’s payload can be moved into another’s destination; partial-content races defeat the crash-safe write guarantee the doc describes.

findings.title: ExportCsvAsync is async void with unobserved exceptions
findings.description: An async void background method cannot be awaited and unobserved exceptions terminate the process. It also ignores its dir/name/links data after writing a constant header, but the concurrency hazard is the async void signature. Scenario: a transient IO failure in File.WriteAllTextAsync becomes an unhandled exception that crashes the service.

findings.title: RequireAdmin always returns true, bypassing admin-only checks
findings.description: RequireAdmin returns true on both branches, so any caller passes the admin gate regardless of role. Combined with Program.AdminQuotas trusting a client-supplied X-Admin header, an authenticated (or token-guessing) attacker reaches admin-only functionality.

findings.title: AdminQuotas trusts a spoofable X-Admin header instead of the session
findings.description: Access control for /admin/quotas is decided by a request header that any client can set to 'true'. Anyone who can present any token that passes auth.Verify reaches the admin endpoint.

findings.title: Session tokens generated with insecure System.Random
findings.description: random.Next() is not cryptographically secure and is seeded from a predictable value, so minted tokens can be predicted and sessions hijacked. The token space is effectively enumerable.

findings.title: DELETE /links does not enforce ownership (IDOR)
findings.description: The handler deletes by caller-supplied code without checking that the link's Owner matches the authenticated session, despite the comment claiming otherwise. Any authenticated user can delete any link, destroying other users' data.

findings.title: Path traversal via user-controlled report name
findings.description: ExportCsv builds path = Path.Combine(dir, name + '.csv') without validating name. A name like '../../etc/cron.d/x' escapes ExportDir; ReadReport uses the same construction, allowing arbitrary file read. ArchiveAll has an analogous issue using owner as filename.

findings.title: Short codes minted with predictable System.Random
findings.description: NewCode uses random.Next(), so generated codes are predictable and enumerable, defeating the unguessability of short links and enabling enumeration of all links.

findings.title: Open redirect in /out via unvalidated next parameter
findings.description: The Location header is set directly from ?next= with no validation, allowing phishing via an open redirect on the service origin.

findings.title: Verify ignores session expiry
findings.description: Verify returns a session matching the token without checking ExpiresAt, so issued tokens never expire and can be used indefinitely.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback secret when LINKD_SECRET is unset
findings.description: When the env var is missing the service silently uses 'dev-secret-do-not-use', a known value shared across all default deployments.

findings.title: Password hashing uses fast unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: HashPassword is plain SHA-256 with no salt or work factor, making stored hashes trivially crackable and identical passwords produce identical hashes.

findings.title: Reports written with default (world-readable) file permissions
findings.description: Despite the comment restricting reads to the service user, StreamWriter uses the process umask with no chmod, so reports containing every owner's links may be world-readable.

findings.title: Snapshot uses a shared predictable /tmp path (TOCTOU/symlink)
findings.description: WriteSnapshot writes to /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json, a predictable path in a world-writable directory, enabling symlink/hardlink races and corruption by another local user.

findings.title: Permissive CORS with credentials enabled
findings.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin '*' combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials 'true' is a dangerous configuration that can enable cross-origin authenticated requests in misbehaving clients.

findings.title: Session tokens written to console log
findings.description: Issued tokens are printed to Console, leaking live credentials to logs and terminal capture.

findings.title: SecretEquals uses non-constant-time comparison
findings.description: Despite the doc comment, presented == expected short-circuits, leaking prefix match information via timing.

findings.title: Presented (invalid) token reflected in 401 response
findings.description: The 401 body echoes the submitted token back, leaking client input and aiding reflection probing by downstream consumers.
